lines.text: Many learners say: Ana is a nurse. She loves his job.
Better: Ana is a nurse. She loves her job.
Ana is a woman, so we say her.
Her! She loves her own job.

data.wrong: Ana is a nurse. She loves his job.
data.right: Ana is a nurse. She loves her job.
data.why: Ana is a woman, so we say her.

quiz.stem: Ana is a nurse. She loves ___ own job.

native.tip: En español “su trabajo” sirve para él y para ella, pero en inglés dices “his” o “her”: “Ana is a nurse. She loves her job.”
native.caption: Muchos dicen “Ana is a nurse. She loves his job.” 🙈 En español “su” sirve para él y para ella, pero en inglés usas “his” o “her” según quién sea el dueño: “Ana is a nurse. She loves her job.” ¡Escucha a Carlos y repite! Practica más en la app Lexkite.
native.comment: Respuesta: “her”. Ana es una mujer, así que va “her”. Escribe una frase tuya con “his” o “her”. Practica más con un quiz gratis aquí: {link}

en.tip: In Spanish “su” works for him and for her, but in English you choose “his” or “her”: “Ana is a nurse. She loves her job.”
en.caption: Many learners say “Ana is a nurse. She loves his job.” In Spanish “su” works for him and for her, but in English you choose “his” or “her” by the owner: “Ana is a nurse. She loves her job.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
